## Body

**Performance: BLOCK P197-F001 / P197-F002** at `f105c6c1547307c12ee760e7ea69772c0b38e687`.

F139's successful within-grace brake and successful final settlement reduce the intended work, but failed settlement can restore the fast retry, and a recorded prime route can cold-wake on replay. These are resource/correctness issues, not same-user identity defenses under C33.

**Waiting-job cost before/after**

| Path | Source-derived cost |
|---|---|
| Before, gone terminal owner | Each 100 ms inspection takes job lookup, completion-event once-guard and owner lookup: nominally 30 logical lookup paths/s/job. Schema checks, done/timed-out tail preparation and completion-history visits are additional; this is not a disk-I/O measurement or a fixed visited-row count. |
| After, within 24-hour grace | One memory deadline/hash/lock test per tick. Between allowed looks, reconcile and those job-specific lookup/notify paths are skipped. On expiry, they run once and the deadline advances 60 s: nominally 3 lookup paths/minute, approximately 0.05/s, plus their existing preparation/guards. |
| Shared work, both versions | `pending()` still executes before the brake, selects and decodes **all current pending job rows** every tick. Waiting-row hydration and its field bytes therefore remain at the shared 100 ms rate until settlement. “Zero reads between looks” only describes incremental per-job paths, not this global read. |
| Successful past-grace settlement | Recorded-route lookup, one-time prime/ancestor/role/project and warmth selection if needed, notice encoding/record write, delivery or Telegram queue admission, then notified write. Once notified, the terminal row leaves `pending`; revive does not redeliver. |

The completion once-guard still scans the relevant owner's completion-kind history for its message ID; its cost is not necessarily one constant-size row. For an owner still present, the new `owner_for` read precedes the existing `finish_source` owner read, adding one owner lookup on that events-completion attempt. The in-memory recheck map is per waiting job and resets at restart. A poisoned lock deliberately disables this brake.

**P197-F001: past-grace failure loses the minute brake.** `notify` calls `forget_owner_recheck` immediately before `settle_orphan` (`background.rs:1476-1477`). The latter can fail in route selection, handoff persistence, Telegram queue admission or `mark_notified`. It returns the error while the job remains unnotified and the cache has no next-look deadline. The next 100 ms tick therefore repeats job lookup, completion guard, owner lookup, handoff and failed settlement work. Recording the route/message ID does not throttle retries.

The real Telegram routing method is a fallible queue enqueue (`bg_routing.rs:143-153`), not proof that the human received it. The fixture already supports a `telegram queue unavailable` failure, but the supplied new orphan tests use successful admissions. This failure path can preserve the read storm F139 is intended to end.

**Required:** retain/schedule the recheck brake while a known-gone job's settlement remains pending, including failed orphan admission/persistence/notified writes; clear it on completed settlement or the appropriate owner transition. Add a past-grace failed-Telegram/settlement regression: ticks inside the minute must not repeat per-job reads/admission, and a later allowed retry settles once. Do not mark a failed notice successful just to remove the row.

**P197-F002: stored “warm prime” is not warm proof on replay.** `settle_orphan` decodes an existing Prime route without calling `escalation`/`prime_route` again (`:1553-1589`), then directly calls `delivery.accept` (`:1592-1601`). A crash after recording the route but before admission can leave it for a much later retry, when the selected prime is cold. That retry can then open the expensive cold turn despite the warm-prime-or-Telegram policy.

**Required:** preserve already-admitted delivery/idempotency, but do not authorize a new prime admission using stale recorded warmth. Test a recorded-but-unadmitted Prime route whose target becomes cold before replay; no cold prime wake should occur, with any wait/downgrade handled consistently with the recorded route rule.

The new policy sits before the command/events split, so both kinds and unknown owners are covered on the successful paths. Notice/record preparation is data-sized. No new direct executable site, timer or poll is introduced, but newly eligible one-time prime delivery can use existing launch adapters; Telegram is an existing queue path. All six spawn guards pass. Bobcat independently corroborated the shared pending-row cost and stale prime-warmth seam; its other correctness/rendering blocks are separate.

Metadata pins the full head; JUnit contains **2,303 executed cases passed**, zero failures/errors/skips, with five separately skipped by nextest. Verified past-grace success, within-grace minute recheck, revive-after-settle, command-job and no-seat Telegram cases, plus six spawn guards. Rust lint, Node22/24 and both delivers runs succeed. These happy/grace cases do not cover the two blockers; author mutants were not rerun.
